what_its_for: Adagrasib is a cancer medicine used to treat a certain type of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) that has spread to other parts of the body. It works specifically in patients whose cancer has a change (mutation) in a gene called KRAS G12C. Your doctor will test your tumor to make sure this medicine is right for you.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablets whole with or without food. Do not crush, break, or chew the tablets. Try to take your doses at the same times each day to help you remember. If you vomit after taking a dose, do not take an extra dose — just take your next scheduled dose at the regular time.
dosing: The usual dose is 2 tablets (400 mg each, for a total of 800 mg) taken twice a day, about 12 hours apart. Always follow the exact dose your doctor prescribes, as your doctor may change your dose if you have side effects.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — BUT only if your next scheduled dose is more than 6 hours away. If your next dose is less than 6 hours away, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store adagrasib at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it in its original container and away from moisture, heat, and direct sunlight. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about proper disposal.
what_to_avoid: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice while taking this medicine, as it can increase the amount of drug in your blood and cause more side effects. Avoid medications that can interact with adagrasib — always tell your doctor and pharmacist about ALL medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, including over-the-counter drugs. Avoid becoming pregnant or fathering a child while on this medicine, as it can harm an unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 6 months after your last dose (females) or 3 months (males).
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: chest pain, fast or irregular heartbeat, dizziness or fainting (which may be signs of a serious heart rhythm problem); severe nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea that is not controlled with medicines; signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain; unusual tiredness or weakness; vision changes or eye pain; or any new or worsening symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: Most patients do not feel adagrasib working right away. It is working inside your body even if you do not notice immediate changes. Your doctor will monitor your progress with scans and lab tests. It may take several weeks to months before your doctor can tell how well the medicine is working for you. Keep taking it as directed even if you feel well.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: This medicine can harm an unborn baby. Do not use if you are pregnant. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine and for at least 1 week after your last dose. Liver problems: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose if you have moderate to severe liver disease. Older adults (65+): No special dose adjustment is usually needed, but you may be more sensitive to side effects — report any unusual symptoms to your doctor promptly. Children: The safety and effectiveness of adagrasib in children has not been established.
